summary: McGill University's Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program funds master's study in Montreal for citizens living in African countries who have not yet started a master's degree.
covers: Full funding for a McGill master's degree, including tuition and living costs.
Leadership development and support for transition into work.
A cohort of Scholars and access to the wider Mastercard Foundation network.
eligibility: Citizens of an African country who are resident in an African country.
Applicants who have never registered for a master's degree.
Dual citizens and permanent residents of the USA, Canada, the UK or the EU are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Check the programme page for the eligible master's programmes and the current recruitment cycle.
The autumn 2027 cohort has closed; the next recruitment cycle is expected to be announced in spring 2027.
Apply to your McGill programme and the Scholars Program as the call instructs.
watch_out: The residence and citizenship rules are strict — check them before you start.
Recruitment runs in cycles and may not open every year.
Montreal is French-speaking; many programmes are in English, but daily life is easier with some French.

costs: On-campus housing and a personal monthly stipend
Academic tools, plus pre-arrival and immigration support
Waived for applicants who pass the scholarship's pre-screening
documents: Attend a programme information session to receive the application link — the scholarship application comes first, before any McGill application
Proof that you are a citizen of, and live in, an African country, and a valid passport
A bachelor's degree closely related to your chosen programme — First Class Honours or equivalent strengthens your case
Evidence of leadership and service, and of how financial constraints have limited your education
Pre-screening documents when asked. If you pass, you receive a fee waiver and instructions to apply to McGill

faq.a: Yes. You must be 35 or younger when you apply.

faq.q: I have already started a master's degree. Can I apply?
faq.a: No. Applicants must never have registered for, or completed, a master's degree.

faq.q: When is the next chance to apply?
faq.a: The fall 2027 cohort has closed; McGill says to check back in spring 2027 for the next cycle. The programme runs from 2024 to 2034 across 13 master's programmes (11 non-thesis, 2 thesis).
